title: PJ Half Marathon Review: What the 2025 Edition Was Like
seo_title: PJ Half Marathon Review: The 2025 Edition | Petaling Jaya
meta_description: PJ Half Marathon review: the 35th edition in 2025 drew 8,000 runners from 34 countries. The 2026 race was cancelled for haze at the last minute.
dek: Petaling Jaya's city half marathon was cancelled at the last minute in September 2026 because of haze. Here is what the last edition that was actually run, in August 2025, was like.
verdict: The PJ Half Marathon is one of the oldest road races in Malaysia. The 2025 edition, on 17 August, was its 35th, and it attracted 8,000 runners, including more than 250 from abroad, across five categories from Laman MBPJ [3]. The 2026 race, moved to 6 September, never happened. Petaling Jaya City Council cancelled it at the last minute because the air quality was still unhealthy [1][2], and the event terms generally make entry fees non-refundable when a race is cancelled for unavoidable reasons [2]. It remains a well-established city race, but after 2026 you should read the refund terms before you enter.

sections.heading: The 2026 Race That Did Not Happen
paragraphs: Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) called off the PJ Half Marathon 2026, due on Sunday 6 September, on safety and health grounds because air quality remained at an unhealthy level [1]. In its statement the council said the forecast suggested the Air Pollutant Index might improve over the following 24 hours, but that the reading was still in the unhealthy range, and that the safety of the running community had to come first [1].

The decision came at the 11th hour [2]. The Star reported that the event's terms state entry fees are generally non-refundable if a race is cancelled for unavoidable circumstances [2]. The council pointed participants to an alternative 5 km route and to arrangements for collecting their race entitlements [1].

PJ was not alone. The same weekend, four Para Sukma events in Selangor were postponed and the Merdeka Spirit Run in Kuching was moved to October, while some other runs in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor went ahead [2]. This was a regional haze episode, not a problem with this race's organisation.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition: 35 Years and 34 Nations
paragraphs: The last PJ Half Marathon to be run was the 35th edition, on 17 August 2025, at Laman MBPJ [3]. Ahead of the race, 8,000 runners had entered, more than 250 of them international participants from 34 countries [3].

It offered five categories: a 30 km, the 21 km half marathon, a 10 km, a 5 km fun run and a 1 km costume run [3]. The event was organised by MBPJ and Puncak Ventures SRA, in collaboration with the Selangor para athletics association [3].

sections.heading: How the 2025 Race Was Run
paragraphs: Race morning started at 2.30am with a warm-up, and staggered flag-offs began at 3.30am with the 30 km [3]. Roads across selected parts of Petaling Jaya were closed from 4am to 11am, and more than 180 enforcement officers and medical staff, including medics on motorcycles, were stationed along the route [3].

Plan for the early start. Almost all of the running happens in the dark, which keeps the heat down but means leaving your hotel in the small hours. Pacemakers Malaysia were the official pacers [3], which helps if you are chasing a particular half-marathon time.

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Next One?
paragraphs: If you live in the Klang Valley, yes. The race has 35 years of history behind it, a big field, a range of distances from 1 km to 30 km, and a city council as organiser.

If you are travelling in, the 2026 cancellation is the thing to weigh. A race in the August to September haze window can be called off at the last minute, and the entry fee may not come back [2]. Book flights and rooms you can change.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2025 edition and on the cancellation of the 2026 race. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: Why was the PJ Half Marathon 2026 cancelled?
faqs.answer: Because of the haze. Petaling Jaya City Council cancelled the 6 September 2026 race at the last minute on safety and health grounds, because the Air Pollutant Index was still in the unhealthy range.

faqs.question: Do you get a refund if the PJ Half Marathon is cancelled?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The Star reported that the event's terms state entry fees are generally non-refundable if the race is cancelled because of unavoidable circumstances. The council did arrange an alternative 5 km route and the collection of race entitlements for 2026.

faqs.question: How big was the PJ Half Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: The 35th edition, on 17 August 2025, had 8,000 runners entered, including more than 250 international participants from 34 countries, across 30 km, 21 km, 10 km, 5 km and 1 km categories.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the last edition that was actually run (17 August 2025), after the 2026 race was cancelled for haze. Replaces a pre-race preview. The 2025 figures are the organisers' pre-race numbers; no post-race report on that edition was found. No rating: nothing here is participant evidence.
